documents.abstract: Memory enables language model assistants to maintain continuity across sessions and generate personalized responses, but knowing more about a user does not necessarily produce responses they prefer. Existing evaluations assess memory capabilities without directly establishing whether memory use benefits the user. To study this gap, we collect approximately 1,000 pairwise judgments from 87 participants using their own ChatGPT queries and personal memories. We find that memory-conditioned responses are not consistently preferred over responses generated without memory and in some cases, users strongly prefer the latter. Automatic evaluators also show limited agreement with users and favor memory-conditioned responses substantially more often than users do. Motivated by these gaps, we introduce a memory-aware reward model that learns from user judgments, achieving 72.8\% preference prediction accuracy and outperforming the existing baselines. Our findings motivate evaluation and optimization objectives that align memory use with the preferences of the people whose information is being used.

Generative AI imposes new metacognitive demands on knowledge workers as their work shifts from production to planning, evaluation, and orchestration. In a randomized, between-subjects experiment on AI-assisted writing (297 workers, 594 essays), we test dynamically-generated metacognitive scaffolds supporting goal specification and task decomposition. We find that scaffolds improve writing quality, with this boost persisting in short-lag transfer when scaffolds are removed. We also find evidence of improved topic recall three days later. These effects are consistent with observed changes in how people learn to prompt AI systems after exposure to scaffolding. However, scaffolded participants rate the AI as less helpful and more cognitively demanding even as they perform better, suggesting that subjective ease can understate the value of support. Our findings make the case for metacognitive scaffolds in AI-assisted knowledge work, revealing a productive friction worth designing for as workers increasingly delegate work to agentic AI.

Wind power is the largest renewable energy source used at the sustainable utility scale. However, wind turbine design, siting, forecasting, control, and maintenance face real challenges, mainly because wind speed is variable and poorly predictable. Over the last ten years, researchers have applied both artificial intelligence (AI) models and metaheuristic optimization algorithms across all phases of the wind energy value chain. This review examines these two methodological approaches across four application fields, with particular attention to evaluation practice, validation level, and implications for sustainability. First, we review wind speed and power forecasting, from statistical baselines to machine learning and deep learning architectures, including models that rely on metaheuristics to tune their hyperparameters and decomposition stages. Second, we examine control applications, focusing on metaheuristic tuning of generator and converter controllers (mainly rotor-side control of doubly-fed induction generators), pitch and torque control, and maximum power point tracking (MPPT). Third, we discuss design-level optimization, covering blade aerodynamic design and wind farm layout under wake effects. Fourth, we examine machine-learning-based supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) monitoring and fault diagnosis, including normal-behavior modelling and anomaly detection. Finally, as floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs) are a cross-cutting emerging field, with coupled hydro-aero-elastic problems in control co-design and AI-based monitoring, the paper proposes a research agenda for the next sustainable generation of onshore and offshore wind systems, focused on standardized open benchmarks, uncertainty-aware forecasting, physics-informed learning, and hardware-validated optimization.

The aim of the article is to reconstruct the lay conceptions held by students of early childhood and pre-primary education regarding generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and its potential role in education. The study is grounded in the constructivist-interpretive paradigm, adopting an understanding of learning as a process of active construction and negotiation of meanings. The empirical material was collected using a questionnaire consisting of open, exploratory questions. The participants were students who had already completed coursework related to didactics but had not yet taken courses on modern technologies. A non-probability purposive sampling strategy was applied. The collected data were analyzed using interpretative thematic analysis. The results reveal tension in students’ common understandings of GenAI. On the one hand, GenAI is perceived as a tool that increases teacher effectiveness and facilitates access to information. On the other hand, the same feature raises concerns about limiting students’ cognitive independence. The results further suggest that future teachers’ ways of thinking about GenAI may be closely related to their understanding of the nature of learning and educational culture. Therefore, the study highlights the need to incorporate reflection on GenAI into teacher education – not as a technical issue, but as a didactic one.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Long-text image-text alignment is essential for fine-grained scene understanding, yet existing methods mainly focus on extending context length or improving local alignment. We identify an overlooked failure mode, saliency collapse, where models over-rely on text that features visual prominence while underutilizing non-salient context. Consequently, retrieval performance degrades sharply when salient content is reduced, despite that the non-salient context remains informative. To address this, we propose RoSA, a saliency-aware finetuning framework that decomposes image-text pairs into complementary salient and contextual views, enabling joint learning of prominent and contextual semantics. We propose a modality-independent decomposition strategy to combine object-level visual saliency estimation with LLM-based text decomposition to bridge vision and language. We employ auxiliary objectives to explicitly align these views, ensuring robust representation with both salient and contextual features. RoSA greatly improves long-text retrieval and demonstrates strong robustness to saliency collapse across benchmarks. Moreover, our auxiliary objectives are plug-and-play, bringing consistent gains to existing tuning methods. Code and checkpoints are available at: https://github.com/intelligolabs/RoSA.
topics: Advanced Image and Video Retrieval Techniques

documents.abstract: Introduction: Physiotherapy education in India is transitioning to a competency-based curriculum that emphasises selfdirected learning. Academic motivation is a key learner-related factor that influences academic outcomes. However, evidence on motivational profiles across academic performance groups remains limited, especially among physiotherapy students. Understanding these differences may facilitate targeted educational support to improve academic outcomes. Aim: To assess academic motivation and compare advanced, average, and Slow Performers (SLP) among undergraduate physiotherapy students. Materials and Methods: The present multicentre crosssectional study was conducted from March 2025 to December 2025 in private physiotherapy colleges affiliated with Maharashtra University of Health Sciences located in Mumbai and Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. A complete enumerative sampling technique was used to recruit 509 eligible first-year physiotherapy undergraduates. Students who took the first formative exam were included. Based on exam scores, students were classified as advanced (top 20%), average (middle 60%), or SLPs (bottom 20%). Data were collected using the Academic Motivation Scale via Google Forms and Analysed applying the Mann-Whitney U test and Kruskal-Wallis H test with Bonferroni correction (p<0.017). A p-value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: A total of 450 participants were included for the final analysis, comprising 74 males (16.44%) and 376 females (83.56%). Significant differences were observed among the three academic performance groups for intrinsic motivation to know (H=13.25, p=0.001) and amotivation (H=13.97, p=0.001). Post-hoc analysis showed significant differences in intrinsic motivation to know between advanced and SLPs, and between average and SLPs, while amotivation differed significantly between advanced and SLPs. Conclusion: The findings of the present study demonstrate that advanced performers exhibited higher intrinsic and lower amotivation than SLPs, although the differences were small. Moreover, extrinsic motivation types did not differ. Integrating early assessment of academic motivation and autonomysupportive learning environments may help reduce amotivation and enhance learner engagement.

Natural-language interfaces allow users to command robotic systems without interacting directly with mission planners or robotics middleware. Their reliable use depends on robot tool routing, defined here as the selection of the smallest complete subset of predefined executable capabilities required to satisfy a request. This task is particularly difficult for compound instructions, where incomplete selection may omit necessary sensing or monitoring capabilities, while excessive selection may expose irrelevant tools. We compare four routing strategies: three progressively refined ChromaDB-based methods - fixed-threshold retrieval, relative-distance retrieval, and clause-aware aggregated retrieval - and a cloud-hosted 120-billion-parameter language-model baseline. The methods are evaluated on 164 manually annotated prompts organised into three complexity levels, from direct single-tool requests to compound requests requiring at least three tools. Using exact-match accuracy, completeness, precision, a completeness-weighted composite score, and routing latency, CDB-v3 achieves the best macro-average score among the retrieval-only methods, with 0.7822, compared with 0.8869 for the large-model baseline. Although the LLM provides higher routing quality, CDB-v3 exhibits substantially lower latency and can be deployed locally without requiring cloud connectivity. These results identify a quality-latency trade-off between direct large-model selection and clause-aware semantic retrieval for privacy-sensitive, connectivity-constrained, and resource-constrained robotic systems.

With the worldwide vertical farming market expected to reach US$33.02 billion by 2030, rising at a compound annual growth rate of 25.1% from 2022 to 2030, vertical farming is becoming increasingly important as a key solution to handle food insecurity, urbanization, and climate change. This chapter investigates how artificial intelligence (AI) and nanotechnology might improve vertical farming systems. By means of technologies including nano-fertilizers, nano-pesticides, and nanosensors, which improve nutrient delivery efficiency by 20–30% and hence lower agrochemical waste by up to 50%, nanotechnology enables precision agriculture. AI algorithms, through machine learning and computer vision, enable real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, and automated decision making simultaneously, so increasing crop yields by up to 35% and lowering resource consumption (water, electricity, and labor). Integration of nanoscale materials with AI-driven analytics helps to create intelligent farming ecosystems, therefore optimizing environmental controls and enhancing food quality in small urban environments. The synergistic possibilities of these technologies, current developments, implementation difficulties, and their combined influence on the direction of smart agriculture and urban food sustainability are covered in this chapter.
topics: Innovations in Aquaponics and Hydroponics Systems
Human Resource Development and Performance Evaluation

documents.abstract: This qualitative study examined how secondary school English teachers in Philippine public schools negotiate and reconstruct pedagogy in response to artificial intelligence (AI). Using Constructivist Grounded Theory, the study drew on intensive semi-structured interviews with seven English teachers from selected public secondary schools under the Schools Division Office of Batangas City. Initial and focused coding, constant comparison, memo writing, and theoretical integration generated seven interrelated categories: continually recalibrating pedagogical practice; protecting the learning work from technological substitution; reconstructing assessment to make learning and authorship visible; negotiating ethical boundaries through contextual professional judgment; building adaptive capacity through collegial and institutional support; cultivating critical AI literacy while preserving human voice and communication; and mediating AI access to preserve equity and inclusive participation. Findings indicate that responsible adaptation involves recursive, context-sensitive professional judgment. Teachers evaluated whether AI supported intended competencies, preserved valid assessment and authorship, maintained ethical safeguards, and enabled equitable participation. The categories informed the emergent AI-Responsive English Pedagogy Framework. The study concludes that responsible integration requires bounded technological augmentation, professional learning, flexible institutional guidance, assessment redesign, and protection of authentic language learning.

As large language models (LLMs) are deployed in interacting populations, their collective behaviour depends not only on the models but also on who interacts with whom. Studies of convention formation in LLM populations have mainly tested well-mixed interactions. We place policies extracted from four LLMs on fully connected, random regular, and heterogeneous networks, with $10^3$ to $10^5$ agents playing the naming game. Topology affects how quickly consensus emerges, sometimes whether it emerges at all, and, in rare cases, which convention wins. Sparsest networks slow consensus up to twelvefold. Yet, by preserving correlations between persistent neighbours, they restore consensus in some cases that fail to converge under well-mixed interactions. Networks also govern vulnerability to adversarial attack. We measure the critical mass of committed agents needed to overturn an established convention. Tipping thresholds follow the same ordering across models and conditions: hubs $\leq$ random $\leq$ low-degree nodes. On the most heterogeneous topology, median critical masses are 3%, 16%, and 35%, respectively; targeting hubs requires one-sixth as many committed agents as random placement. For most models, networked populations are easier to tip than well-mixed ones, so well-mixed estimates can overstate robustness. Assessing the safety of multi-agent AI requires mapping who interacts with whom.

G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) modulate diverse hormonal, metabolic, neural, and immunological signaling processes. Their age-dependent decline accounts for many fundamental hallmarks of aging, including low-grade inflammation (inflammaging), mitochondrial failure and energy dysregulation, genomic instability and epigenetic dysregulation, dysregulated cellular communication, loss of proteostasis, and cellular senescence. Consequently, GPCR dysfunction underpins nearly all chronic, age-related diseases, including cardiovascular disease, cancer, various endocrine disorders, and neurodegenerative conditions such as Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases. Therefore, the GPCR network (“GPCR-ome”) constitutes a central, druggable, “mega-trophic” regulator of human healthspan. Individual GPCRs present numerous therapeutic targets for specific conditions, many of which are already being exploited, while others show future promise. Alongside this disease-centric approach, the GPCR-ome offers the more radical opportunity to rebalance entire signaling networks to simultaneously correct the multisystem pathological effects of aging itself. Here, we outline a transformative paradigm for network-level, GPCR-based geroprotection that employs artificial intelligence, digital twins, and quantum computational methods to design biased agonists, allosteric or multitarget modulators, heteromer-selective ligands, and polypharmacological strategies to mitigate and manage age-related disorders. We also explore how combinatorial GPCR-based strategies (e.g., coupled with senolytic, metabolic, or regenerative medicines) hold compelling promise to delay multiple hallmarks of aging and enable personalized anti-aging GPCR therapies based on multiomic biomarkers.
topics: Genetics, Aging, and Longevity in Model Organisms

documents.abstract: This working paper presents Neuroforge Interactive Learning V1, a reproducible pilot study of rule identification through binary success/failure feedback. The experiment evaluates a symbolic learning agent against a fixed, non-learning baseline across 100 seeded episodes, with 16 actions per episode (1,600 actions per policy). The fixed baseline achieved 25.50% action accuracy (408/1,600), while the feedback-learning agent achieved 91.94% (1,471/1,600). All four automated tests passed in the local evaluation. The learner identifies an active rule from four predefined candidates using feedback. Its memory resets between episodes. The experiment does not establish neural-network learning, general artificial intelligence, autonomous discovery of arbitrary rules, or transfer to previously unseen rule families. The paper documents the experimental setup, observed results, limitations, and proposed future work toward interactive rule discovery and cross-task generalization. This is an independently authored, non-peer-reviewed research working paper associated with QuantEdge AI LLC.

Interactive 3D segmentation models such as nnInteractive turn a few spatial prompts (points, scribbles, boxes) into accurate volumetric masks, but a human still does the annotation work: finding each structure, placing prompts, checking the result and correcting it. General-purpose AI agents can now interpret images, call tools and write code. We show that such agents can take over this work without additional training: the user makes a request in plain language, and the agent works out what has to be segmented, locates the targets, prompts nnInteractive, inspects the 3D result, corrects it and responds to feedback. Asked for 'the muscles used for chewing', an agent identifies and segments the masseters and pterygoids; asked to count liver lesions, it writes its own code to find candidates and splits a merged lesion on request. Our open-source nninteractive-agent provides nnInteractive as tools over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), together with a skill that encodes how experienced users prompt it. On a benchmark spanning CT, MRI, PET and micro-CT of humans, a mouse and an ant (14 images; 51 targets from organs and tumours to muscles, foot bones, vessel trees and an insect brain), Claude Code and Codex reach a mean Dice of 0.81 and 0.84 from the request alone; when told where each target is, both reach 0.85 and prompt nearly as effectively as an oracle that places prompts using the reference segmentation. A text-prompted 3D model (VoxTell) is more accurate on most standard radiological targets but less robust: it returns an empty mask for one of them and fails on the leg muscles, the foot bones, the mouse and the ant, where the agents remain accurate. Code: https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nninteractive-agent
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Abstract The NOAA-NASA Joint Archive (NNJA pronounced like the word ninja) is a publicly accessible, curated collection of Earth system observations spanning 1979 to present, created to accelerate reanalysis production, support development of artificial intelligence (AI) applications, and enable access to the observational record underlying modern reanalyses. The archive encompasses atmospheric satellite radiances and conventional measurements, in-situ ocean profiles, sea ice concentrations and freeboard retrievals, and land surface observations from over 60 sensors provided by NOAA, NASA, and their partners. The number of atmospheric records increases from around 10 6 observations per day in 1979 to around 10 8 in the modern era. The dataset extends into near-real time through continuous archival of the NOAA operational data. NNJA observations are distributed through Amazon Web Services in formats compatible with established data assimilation systems and are accompanied by channel-level black and white lists that capture the quality history of the satellite record. Data integrity is verified through a three-tier process: file-level metadata checks, cross-validation against existing black and white lists from prior NOAA and NASA reanalyses, and a comparison of assimilation statistics with reference reanalysis and operational products. To lower barriers for the machine learning community, a companion dataset (NNJA-AI) transforms NNJA observations from legacy formats to column-oriented Apache Parquet, enabling sufficient large-scale queries and direct integration with AI training workflows. This article describes the creation, verification, and curation of the NNJA dataset, document its current scope and known limitations, and discusses its role as a shared observational infrastructure for the next generation of U.S. reanalyses.

Numerical analysis serves as the fundamental pillar of modern engineering modeling, providing the mathematical and computational tools necessary to transform complex physical equations into practical numerical solutions. This study reviews contemporary applications of numerical analysis in enhancing engineering models, focusing on methodological advancements in solving partial differential equations, data-driven model order reduction techniques, adaptive mesh methods, and machine learning-based surrogate models. The study employs a synthetic analytical approach that combines a review of recent literature with an analysis of empirical results from various numerical methods, addressing hybrid models that integrate traditional techniques with artificial intelligence. The analysis demonstrates that combining traditional numerical analysis methods with artificial intelligence and reduced-order models has revolutionized the ability of engineers to simulate complex multiphysics systems with unprecedented accuracy and computational efficiency; hybrid models have achieved computational speedups ranging from 72 to 522 times compare to traditional methods. Furthermore, the study addresses challenges related to computational cost and solution sensitivity to initial conditions, examining cutting-edge innovative solutions such as physicsinformed neural networks and causality-based learning. The study concludes that future trends in this field are shifting towards the development of hybrid models that combine analytical accuracy with computational speed, with an increasing emphasis on generalization capabilities beyond the training data. This opens up broad prospects for digital engineering and digital twin applications across the industrial, energy, and infrastructure sectors. The study offers a comprehensive perspective on the development of engineering models using advanced numerical analysis techniques and identifies promising future research directions in this vital field.
topics: Advanced Numerical Methods in Computational Mathematics

documents.abstract: This article examines the motivational, individual psychological, social, and organizational-pedagogical factors influencing the development of students' intellectual abilities through metacognitive strategies. A total of 280 students from the 7th and 9th grades participated in the study. The Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire (MSLQ), developed by P.R. Pintrich, A.F. Smith, T. Garcia, and W.J. McKeachie, along with H. Gardner's Multiple Intelligences assessment method, was used to investigate correlations between motivational factors and different types of intelligence. The findings revealed positive correlations between intrinsic goal orientation, task value, self-efficacy for learning performance, elaboration, critical thinking, and metacognitive self-regulation and linguistic, logical-mathematical, and personal intelligences. Furthermore, the study highlights the significance of students' age-related characteristics, independent thinking, reflective abilities, and the educational environment in the application of metacognitive strategies. The findings substantiate the importance of psychological and pedagogical approaches aimed at strengthening intrinsic motivation, improving self-monitoring, and enhancing reflective activities to promote the development of students' intellectual potential.

Public officials perform diverse administrative, public-facing, emergency, and safety–critical tasks, yet their occupational risk profiles have rarely been characterized across actual job functions. In Korea, public officials have historically remained partly outside core occupational safety and health requirements, and systematic evidence on their occupational risk profiles across diverse job functions has been limited. This study applied the Public Officials’ Occupational Risk Assessment (PORA) tool to 36,779 Korean public officials to screen perceived occupational risks and identify occupation- and job-function-specific high-risk patterns. Respondents assessed exposure frequency and intensity for 24 occupational risk factors across psychological, organizational, ergonomic, physical, chemical, and biological domains. Risk scores were calculated as the product of frequency and intensity, and high-risk responses were defined as “high” or “very high” according to the PORA risk matrix. Prolonged sitting showed the highest mean risk score and high-risk prevalence, followed by public-facing work, fast work pace, time pressure, emotional stress, awkward posture, and repetitive upper-limb work. Frequency–intensity comparisons showed that some risks were driven by frequent exposure, whereas event-based psychological hazards received lower time-proportion-based frequency ratings but relatively higher intensity ratings. Occupation-specific logistic regression showed distinct profiles: general service officials were characterized by prolonged sitting and time pressure, police officers by broad psychological, ergonomic, and physical hazards, and firefighters by physical, chemical, biological, and emergency-response-related hazards. Job-function heatmaps and hierarchical clustering further revealed heterogeneous risk profiles across 22 main job functions. These findings highlight the need for job-function-based, participatory, and risk-prioritized occupational safety and health management in public organizations.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Advances in Omni-modal Large Language Models (OLLMs) have enabled increasingly seamless human-AI interaction, but their unified processing of heterogeneous modalities also expands the attack surface, allowing adversaries to exploit richer input compositions to circumvent safety alignment. To counter such risks, omni-modal guardrails have been proposed to detect and filter unsafe queries across arbitrary modalities. However, their capabilities and limitations remain insufficiently understood due to the absence of a comprehensive evaluation benchmark. In this paper, we present Omni-UBench, the first comprehensive framework for omni-modal safety assessment, evaluating guardrail models along three critical dimensions, i.e., safety, utility, and reliability. Omni-UBench curates over 183k samples drawn from 35+ heterogeneous sources spanning text, image, audio, video, and their cross-modal combinations, annotated with safety labels under a unified risk taxonomy. Benchmarking under Omni-UBench on 15 representative OLLMs and omni-modal guardrails yields several key findings, including: (1) modern OLLMs exhibit strong content moderation potential even without guardrail-specific tuning; (2) existing guardrails still struggle to identify cross-modal queries that conceal harmful intent or involve sophisticated jailbreaks; (3) they further exhibit substantial safety hallucination and over-sensitivity to textual patterns, revealing a deficient understanding of cross-modal safety semantics. Our findings provide valuable insights for developing more trustworthy omni-modal guardrails in future research.

Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong reasoning capabilities, motivating their use as the backbone of foundation recommendation models (FRMs). Existing methods enhance recommendations through explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning under a Think-then-Answer paradigm. However, explicit CoT incurs substantial inference overhead by generating lengthy reasoning traces and relies on manually designed templates that struggle to capture diverse, dynamic user interests. We propose OneLatent, an efficient latent reasoning framework that compresses explicit reasoning traces into several learnable latent tokens, enabling Latent-Reason-then-Answer inference without generating verbose traces. OneLatent first introduces Multi-View Adaptive CoT (MV-ACoT), which creates diverse, high-quality teacher-generated supervision by exploring user interests from multiple perspectives and automatically adapting reasoning complexity to each instance. Building on pretrained FRMs, it then uses a three-stage latent-token alignment paradigm to progressively internalize CoT traces into learnable latent tokens. Finally, a multistage curriculum-based post-training strategy activates latent-token reasoning for downstream recommendation tasks. Experiments on an industrial-scale Kuaishou dataset and the public Kuaishou LLM-Rec benchmark show that OneLatent consistently outperforms explicit CoT-based methods and traditional baselines. Compared with the Think and No-Think variants of FRMs, OneLatent improves SID@64 by 17.44% and 9.33%, respectively, while achieving over 17x higher online inference throughput. We further develop a production serving system for scalable, real-time FRM inference. An online A/B test in Kuaishou's local-services advertising scenario shows that deploying OneLatent with this system yields an estimated 9.6% revenue lift over strong online baselines, including OneRec and OneReason.

Abstract Deep visual proteomics (DVP) is an emerging approach for cell-type-specific and spatially resolved proteomics. However, its broad adoption has been constrained by the lack of an open-source end-to-end workflow within a community-driven ecosystem. Here we introduce openDVP, an experimental and computational framework for accessible and scalable DVP. OpenDVP combines open-source image analysis tools (MCMICRO, QuPath and napari) with scverse formats (AnnData and SpatialData) for multiomics integration. It provides two workflows: a fast-track pipeline requiring no image analysis expertise, and an artificial intelligence-powered pipeline incorporating state-of-the-art methods for image preprocessing, segmentation and spatial analysis. We apply openDVP across three archival tissue studies (human placenta, early stage lung cancer and locally relapsed breast cancer), integrating spatial single-cell phenotypes with exploratory proteomic measurements. Finally, we introduce deep proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods as a scalable approach for spatial discovery proteomics.

The relentless exponential scaling of foundation models and transformer architectures has pushed conventional silicon complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) digital accelerators (GPUs, TPUs) toward fundamental thermodynamic and interconnect boundaries. Joule heating, resistance-capacitance (RC) interconnect delay scaling, and the 'memory wall' severely constrain energy efficiency and compute density. Optical Computing and Integrated Silicon Photonics (SiPh) establish an analog non-Von Neumann hardware paradigm that executes fundamental linear algebra operations—specifically General Matrix-Matrix Multiplication (GEMM)—at the speed of light with near-zero runtime energy dissipation. By encoding vector-matrix activations into coherent optical wave fields and modulating light through cascaded Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (MZI) meshes, Micro-Ring Resonator (MRR) banks, and Wavelength-Division Multiplexing (WDM) waveguides, photonic tensor processing units (PTPUs) execute analog matrix multiplications in continuous time with sub-nanosecond propagation latencies. However, translating integrated photonic circuits into production deep learning accelerators introduces profound optoelectronic engineering bottlenecks: analog noise accumulation across deep optical meshes, severe thermal phase drift, limited electro-optic Digital-to-Analog / Analog-to-Digital (DAC/ADC) conversion resolution, non-linear activation implementation hurdles, and wafer-scale optical footprint scaling. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of integrated photonic computing for deep neural network acceleration. We formalize the Clements and Reck unitary matrix decomposition algorithms over reconfigurable MZI topologies, derive the optical transmission transfer matrix under optical carrier phase error perturbations, and establish energy-per-MAC physical thermodynamic bounds across electro-optic conversion interfaces. Furthermore, we construct an empirical co-simulation and hardware testbed benchmarking silicon photonic meshes against state-of-the-art CMOS accelerators (NVIDIA H100, Google TPU v5p) across vision transformers, large language model attention heads, and resonant graph convolutions. Our empirical findings demonstrate that a 64x64 integrated MZI photonic mesh achieves a 58.4x improvement in energy-delay product (EDP) over 4nm digital CMOS cores, sustaining up to 128 Tera-Operations per Second per Watt (TOPS/W) at 4-bit to 8-bit equivalent precision, while active thermo-optic phase stabilization preserves 98.2% baseline classification accuracy. Finally, we establish open research directions in all-optical non-linear activation functions, co-packaged optical memory architectures, and wafer-scale photonic interconnect scaling.

Amid growing water scarcity and losses in distribution networks, it is crucial to find effective solutions that increase efficiency and ensure the sustainability of water management. This global demand is reflected in the regional scenario of the state of Bahia, especially in the capital, Salvador. Data from the Bahia State Basic Sanitation Regulatory Agency (AGERSA) points to recurring problems with water interruptions that are not sufficiently unpredictable. Based on this issue, this article presents a literature review on emerging technologies to improve water supply management in smart cities, with specific application to the capital of Bahia. The methodology employed involves a technical review of the main technologies currently applied in Smart Water Networks, including smart meters and advanced sensors for water quality monitoring, proposing an integrated model based on the Internet of Things (IoT) and Big Data analysis (AI; Machine Learning).The expected results include improved operational efficiency, greater accuracy in early detection and response to critical events such as leaks and supply interruptions, as well as greater transparency of water supply and treatment information for users and managers. The conclusion is that the implementation of the solution will significantly contribute to the technical, operational, and environmental sustainability of urban water systems.

There is very little published research about evidence-based practice (EBP) in occupational health services (OHS), and none to date in Finland. The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) model of evidence-based healthcare provides a clear and intuitive conceptual framework for exploring how research evidence and the practice of medicine could be better integrated. Thus far it has seen very little use within the occupational health arena. This study explores the extent of organisational support given to OHS professionals in providing EBP in Finland. We collected survey data ( n = 524) from Finnish OHS physicians and nurses involved either solely in patient care duties or also in a managerial, development or expert role, using a validated online questionnaire (EBP-OHS) that was made available in two waves: in November 2020 and August 2021. We analysed quantitative data using descriptive methods and qualitative data using content analysis. Most respondents reported that their organisations value evidence-based practice (83%) and encourage staff to use evidence-based information (74%). In their opinion, the most important means to support EBP were managerial support and example, employee training, and a dedicated team or expert responsible for ensuring that care delivery consistently aligns with the latest evidence. The respondents wanted clear and uniform processes for implementing research evidence into practice, and IT systems that support both the implementation and reporting of EBP in practice. Successful EBP in OHS seems likely to require managers to set a good example, both in their attitude and actions. Building a culture of implementing EBP requires staff to be empowered to share and keep up with robust and relevant new evidence and to be allocated sufficient time to do so. OHS units need to have clear structures and forums dedicated to engaging in EBP. OHS would likely benefit from having clear implementation processes and EBP tools that allow systematic follow-up and reporting.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: In talent pathways that formally include both sexes, it remains unclear whether boys and girls selected into the same pathway accumulate comparable football activity. This study aimed to (1) describe sex-stratified self-reported weekly football exposure and motivational regulation among 103 players (51 girls, 52 boys; 13.8 ± 0.9 years) selected for one regional division of a Norwegian national youth talent development program, and (2) describe age-cohort patterns across the ≤13-, 14- and 15-year cohorts. Players reported weekly football hours and sessions during the preparation period and competitive season. Because the dataset lacked club- and training-group identifiers, observations could not be assumed independent; the study is therefore descriptive and exploratory: sex-stratified exposure and motivational regulation are summarized as median [interquartile range, IQR], age-cohort exposure as mean ± SD, and between-sex patterns as differences in central tendency rather than as hypothesis tests. In this sample, boys reported higher total weekly football exposure than girls (median 10.8 vs. 7.0 h), with a proportionally larger difference for self-organized than organized activity. Boys reported slightly higher intrinsic motivation and identified regulation, whereas girls reported slightly higher amotivation, external regulation and introjected regulation; these differences were small relative to the scale range, and both groups reported high intrinsic motivation and low amotivation in absolute terms. Because players were drawn from shared but unmodeled development environments in a cross-sectional design, the findings are descriptive only: equal formal selection did not coincide with equal football exposure, particularly in self-organized activity, generating hypotheses for future cluster-aware studies.

topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: General-purpose embeddings trained on profile similarity often misrank candidates in professional networks, where relevance is inherently complementary rather than symmetric. For example, job seekers usually engage with recruiters rather than peers with similar credentials. Current user recommendation systems are often built on profile similarity or social signals such as shared connections, which are effective in friend-oriented social networks where users tend to connect with similar people or within existing social circles. However, this does not hold in professional platforms like LinkedIn, where interactions are often goal-driven and cross-role interactions, requiring matching based on complementary intents rather than similarity or social proximity. In this paper, we propose Preference-Aligned Intent Retrieval, a retrieval framework that is designed to model user intent preference instead of profile similarity. Our approach is inspired by the preference-learning perspective of Direct Preference Optimization, but instantiates preference learning as an exposure-conditioned multi-negative contrastive objective over embeddings. This formulation simplifies training and scales efficiently to large candidate sets without requiring an explicit reference model. Furthermore, we incorporate user interaction history by aggregating click histories with positional encoding to capture temporal order, which enables constant-cost updates of user representations over a fixed history window, allowing new interactions to be incorporated without re-encoding history. As a result, personalization can be updated efficiently using lightweight CPU operations without repeated LLM inference during serving. We evaluate PAIR on LinkedIn's Premium retrieval task. A 0.6B parameter model achieves a MAR@100 of 0.45.

Bashkir is a low-resource agglutinative language written in Cyrillic and remains poorly represented in modern LLMs. We present an open resource suite and a systematic benchmark of adaptation methods: the Bashkir Web Corpus (71,567 documents, 46.9M tokens, 16 sources) and three labelled datasets for binary, multiclass and multilabel text classification; the benchmark covers the first two. Experiments use eight architectures (82M-8B: DistilGPT2, GPT-2 base/medium, Phi-3-mini, Mistral-7B, YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B, mBERT, XLM-R) and three adaptation groups (full fine-tuning, QLoRA, in-context learning), plus continual pretraining (CPT). (1) QLoRA on 3.8-8B models outperforms encoder-only fine-tuning on binary classification: YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B with CPT reaches macro-F1 0.748 vs 0.653 (XLM-R) and 0.650 (mBERT); pairwise differences are significant after Holm correction (p<0.001). (2) YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B significantly outperforms Mistral-7B and Phi-3-mini on multiclass classification, BPB and native-speaker ratings (mean 3.28 vs 2.52 and 2.22; n=100; alpha=0.69-0.77; p<0.05); on binary classification its QLoRA advantage is not significant (p>=0.084). (3) CPT effects depend on model and task: perplexity improves for Phi-3-mini (+0.58) and YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B (+0.33) but worsens for Mistral-7B (-1.15, p<0.001); on binary classification CPT helps Mistral-7B most (+4.0 macro-F1). (4) Tokeniser fertility on Bashkir varies 2.67x (2.92-7.80) and tracks adaptation quality, while perplexity across tokenisers is not comparable. Cyrillic tokenisers with Russian pretraining are preferable; LLM judges reproduce native ratings for grammar and coherence (rho=0.33-0.46) but not language correctness (rho=0.16, p=0.11); native evaluation remains necessary. All artefacts are open-licensed.

Validation studies of zero-shot language-model scoring of psychological interviews often rely primarily on a single convergent correlation with a questionnaire to establish validity. However, a bivariate correlation cannot reveal whether a model lacks discriminant validity, agrees poorly in absolute terms, produces non-random missing scores, or scores inconsistently. We evaluated eight open-weight families (1–70B active parameters) and eight commercial frontier models. The models scored the same sets of clinical interviews (Study 1: suicide recovery, n = 149; Study 2: future self-continuity, n = 164) across 52 configurations. Convergent validity improves with model size in both studies. However, the standard open-weight models tested achieve only about three-quarters of frontier convergent validity, with 11-fold greater mean absolute bias, more format failures, and lower repeatability in Study 1. In Study 2, standard open models (≤ 27B) are as strongly correlated with a closely related construct (suicide recovery) as with the target (mean difference −0.014), although they correlate less strongly with a distal neighbor (life satisfaction). All six frontier generations correlate more strongly with the target than with either neighbor (mean difference from recovery +0.117). On a local workstation, Gemma 4 31B is within the frontier range on all discriminant validity indices, outperforming its similar-sized predecessor. Llama 3.3 70B shows no greater discriminant validity than Gemma 4 31B, suggesting that discriminant validity is a function of release, not parameter count alone. Based on these findings, we suggest a minimum validation standard across five domains.

On 1 May 2026, six Five Eyes cybersecurity agencies jointly issued Careful Adoption of Agentic AI Services, the first coordinated Anglophone statement on the governance of LLM-based autonomous agents. This Comment argues that, although the Guidance offers competent cybersecurity risk management within its stated remit, its institutional weight invites a broader governance reading that the document cannot bear, and that five structural limitations then come into view. First, the cybersecurity doctrines on which it relies are necessary but insufficient for agentic systems, whose delegated authority, underspecified goals, and long-horizon autonomy strain the assumptions of conventional controls. Second, it privatises systemic risk by imposing duties on deployers without specifying public-law obligations, redress, or liability across the agentic value chain. Third, it prescribes human oversight without specifying the conditions of effective control, so that responsibility risks being assigned to reviewers who lack the information, authority, or time to exercise it. Fourth, it reduces accountability to auditability, confusing a technical property with a legal relation between duty-holders and affected parties. Fifth, the security-defined mandates of its six authoring agencies, and the intelligence-oversight structures within which most of them sit, raise questions of institutional voice, while its Five Eyes-only authorship raises a risk of divergence from the AI frameworks now emerging in the European Union, the Republic of Korea and Japan. The Comment concludes by outlining the elements of an enforceable, rights-protective, cross-jurisdictional legal regime that should supplement, rather than be displaced by, the technical controls the Guidance recommends.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Background: Patient trust may determine whether artificial intelligence (AI) is accepted in dental care, particularly when AI contributes to diagnosis or treatment planning. We aimed to synthesize patient-reported trust, confidence, acceptance, and preferences regarding dental AI and to identify factors associated with these outcomes. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to 2 June 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed with the revised JBI tool for analytical cross-sectional studies. Because outcomes and metrics were heterogeneous, findings were synthesized narratively. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261439049). Results: The final synthesis included eight studies comprising 3171 participants from five countries. Attitudes were generally favourable when AI supported rather than replaced dentists. In one study, 47.7% accepted AI-assisted interpretation of diagnostic data, whereas 10.8% trusted an entirely AI-generated diagnosis. Another study found that 84.9% supported AI analysis of dental images followed by dentist review. A fixed-order vignette study improved lesion recognition but did not significantly change trust in the dentist. Interpretation was limited by non-probability sampling, heterogeneous and often non-validated measures, incomplete control of confounding, and reporting inconsistencies. Conclusions: Available evidence suggests conditional acceptance of dental AI, particularly when dentists retain oversight. Confidence in the prevalence estimates of trust and acceptance is low; these findings do not establish that AI improves trust. More representative studies using validated, conceptually distinct outcome measures are required.

documents.abstract: Abstract Background: Research on teachers' AI use has largely focused on whether teachers use AI or how many purposes they report. These measures cannot show how teachers combine AI across different parts of instructional work or whether professional learning relates differently to those combinations. Objectives: This study identified patterns of professional AI use among lower-secondary teachers and examined whether AI-related professional learning differed across them. Methods: We analysed 2024 Teaching and Learning International Survey (TALIS) data from 25,705 teachers in 54 education systems who reported using AI for teaching or student learning. Equal-system weighted latent class analysis examined eight purposes. Adjusted three-step models related AI-related professional learning to profile membership while accounting for classification uncertainty and teacher characteristics. Results and Conclusions: A four-profile solution was retained: preparation-focused (40.07%), design-and-adaptation-focused (23.87%), data-and-feedback-focused (18.70%), and broad-purpose use (17.37%). Beyond breadth, the two intermediate profiles covered a similar range of purposes but diverged in material adaptation and student-data review. Among professional-learning participants, AI-related rather than non-AI content was associated with higher odds of design-and-adaptation membership (OR = 2.03, 95% CI [1.62, 2.53]) and broad-purpose membership (OR = 2.40, 95% CI [1.99, 2.89]) relative to data-and-feedback membership; broad-purpose and design-and-adaptation membership did not differ significantly. Teacher AI use therefore varies in both breadth and instructional purpose. The findings move beyond overall prevalence and provide a task-based basis for designing and evaluating AI-related professional learning, while leaving its effects on teachers’ practice to be tested longitudinally. Manuscript status Under review at the Journal of Computer Assisted Learning. Registration timing This record documents a completed study. Data analysis and manuscript preparation were completed before this registration, and the manuscript is currently under journal review. This is a retrospective registration, not a prospective preregistration.

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly influencing sustainability education by providing dynamic tools that foster systems thinking, data literacy, ethical reasoning, and creative problem solving. Yet despite growing experimentation with AI in teaching and learning, there remains a notable gap in practice-based frameworks that guide educators in integrating AI into ESD in ethically grounded and pedagogically purposeful ways. Addressing this need, this chapter explores how AI can be thoughtfully integrated into Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) through innovative pedagogical approaches. Drawing on teaching cases and reflective analysis, it introduces the IDEA (Innovation, Design, Evaluation, and Anchoring) framework as a structured yet flexible guide for integrating AI into practice. The framework is illustrated through practice-informed vignettes, including the use of generative AI for futures thinking, machine learning for environmental data analysis, AI-powered feedback in ethics debates, and co-designed projects with pre-service teachers. These examples highlight both the affordances and tensions of using AI in higher education and teacher preparation programs. The IDEA framework encourages educators to critically examine how AI tools align with sustainability goals, support meaningful learning outcomes, and surface issues of ethics, equity, and digital competence. Situating AI not as a disruptive novelty but as a pedagogical mediator, the chapter contributes to the discourse on ESD and the responsible integration of emerging technologies. Drawing on interdisciplinary scholarship, it reflects on implications for curriculum design, faculty development, and education policy, offering actionable recommendations for creating ethical, inclusive, and future-facing learning environments.

This study was initiated by the uneven learning motivation among junior high school students in Coding and Artificial Intelligence (CAI) subjects. The research aims to enhance students’ learning motivation through a project-based gamification strategy. The method employed was Classroom Action Research (CAR) based on the Kemmis and McTaggart model, conducted in two cycles with 31 students as subjects. The learning process implemented Project-Based Learning (PjBL) integrated with six gamification elements (clear goals, points, challenges, badges, feedback, and leaderboards) through a simple Scratch game development project. Data were collected using an adapted Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire (MSLQ), observations, field notes, and documentation, and analyzed descriptively. The results showed an increase in students’ learning motivation, with the classical average rising from 3.06 (76.39%) in the pre-cycle to 3.24 (81.00%) in Cycle I and 3.38 (84.39%) in Cycle II, and all motivation aspects improving. Students reaching the minimum “High” criterion (score ≥ 3.00) increased from 51.61% (16 students) in the pre-cycle to 77.42% (24 students) in Cycle I, and reached the classical success target at 80.65% (25 students) in Cycle II. In Cycle II, a layered troubleshooting strategy using a Generative AI chatbot as a coding assistant, followed by peer feedback, appeared to support more persistent and independent problem-solving, although the gains were moderate and uneven across students, and self-regulation remained the lowest-scoring aspect (3.09). In conclusion, project-based gamification was accompanied by an increase in junior high school students’ learning motivation in CAI subjects.

Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh penerapan model pembelajarn Discovery Learning yang belum terlaksana secara optimal, serta penggunaan Artificial Intelligence dalam pembelajaran yang masih bersifat umum, belum terarah, dan belum dimanfaatkan secara inovatif sebagai pendukung proses belajar peserta didik. Kondisi tersebut menyebabkan peserta didik masih mengalami kesulitan dalam memahami konsep-konsep kimia yang bersifat abstrak. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh penerapan model Discovery Learning berbantuan Artificial Intelligence terhadap hasil belajar peserta didik pada materi teori asam basa. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode pre-experimental design dan desain One Group Pretest-Posttest Design. Sampel penelitian terdiri atas 35 peserta didik kelas X.E di SMK SMAK Makassar yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Teknik pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui tes hasil belajar berupa pretest dan posttest. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan statistik deskriptif dan inferensial melalui uji prasyarat yakni uji normalitas, dilanjutkan uji hipotesis nonparametric yakni Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test, dan analisis N-gain. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penerapan model Discovery Learning berbantuan Artificial Intelligence memberikan pengaruh terhadap peningkatan hasil belajar peserta didik. Nilai N-gain berada pada kategori tinggi sehingga model pembelajaran tersebut efektif dalam meningkatkan hasil belajar peserta didik pada materi teori asam basa.

The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence in the academic world has triggered a new psychological phenomenon known as ailessphobia, defined as anxiety resulting from the loss of access to AI, whose main dimensions are closely related to academic self-efficacy. Nevertheless, empirical evidence regarding the relationship between ailessphobia and academic self-efficacy still demonstrates inconsistent results, whereas self-efficacy itself is a crucial predictor of first-year students' academic adaptation and achievement success. On the other hand, mindfulness is identified as a protective psychological resource that is positively associated with enhanced self-regulation and self-efficacy among students, making it potential to be tested jointly within a single model. Most prior literature regarding these variables remains dominated by engineering and nursing students abroad. Consequently, studies exploring the effect of mindfulness and ailessphobia on academic self-efficacy among Psychology students in Indonesia, specifically at Universitas Negeri Surabaya, have not yet been found. Given that early-semester students are in a crucial transitional period of self-efficacy development, coupled with the availability of locally validated measurement instruments, conducting this study is essential to fill the void in the literature. This study aims to determine and explain the effect of mindfulness and ailessphobia on students' self-efficacy. The focus of this research is to explore whether mindfulness affects students' academic self-efficacy, as well as whether ailessphobia also influences academic self-efficacy. In addition, this study seeks to ascertain whether both factors (mindfulness & ailessphobia) collectively exert a significant influence on students' academic self-efficacy. The objectives of this research are clearly formulated and measurable, as they directly address the proposed problems and can be tested through quantitative research methods. Hyphotheses : Null Hypothesis (H0): Mindfulness and ailessphobia together do not affect academic self-efficacy among early-semester psychology students at UNESA. Alternative Hypothesis (H1): Mindfulness and ailessphobia affect academic self-efficacy among early-semester psychology students at UNESA. Alternative Hypothesis (H2): Mindfulness affects academic self-efficacy among early-semester psychology students at UNESA. Alternative Hypothesis (H3): Ailessphobia affects academic self-efficacy among early-semester psychology students at UNESA. This study is designed using a quantitative approach with a predictive correlational (explanatory) design. This approach was chosen because it aims to explain and measure the extent to which the independent variables, mindfulness (X1) and ailessphobia (X2), are capable of predicting variations in the dependent variable, namely academic self-efficacy ($Y$). Data were collected using a cross-sectional method, in which data collection was conducted within a single timeframe (a one-shot study) via an online questionnaire hosted on PsyToolkit. The cross-sectional approach provides an empirical overview of the relationships between variables without intervening in or manipulating the respondents' conditions, and it is not intended to infer long-term causal relationships. The target population in this study comprises active undergraduate students in the Psychology Department at Universitas Negeri Surabaya (UNESA) who are in the early transition period of higher education (semesters 1 to 4) and have experience using Generative AI technology for academic activities. Inclusion Criteria: -Active undergraduate Psychology students at UNESA in semesters 1 to 4. -Have utilized Generative AI platforms (such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or DeepSeek) to complete assignments or academic activities. -Willing to participate and complete the questionnaire voluntarily (informed consent). Exclusion Criteria: -Respondents with incomplete submission data (missing data). -Respondents exhibiting invalid response patterns (e.g., straight-lining or careless responding). -Duplicate submission data. -Students who were involved in the trial phase (try-out) of the research instruments. Academic Self-Efficacy is measured using The Indonesian Academic Self-Efficacy Scale (TIASS) developed by Darmayanti et al. (2024), based on the theoretical framework of Zajacova et al. (2005). This scale consists of 20 positively phrased items. It measures four main dimensions: (1) Interaction at university, (2) Performance out of class, (3) Performance in class, and (4) Managing work, family, and university. Mindfulness is measured using the Short Version of the Five Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire (FFMQ), adapted by Fourianalistyawati et al. (2023). This scale consists of 10 items (6 favorable items and 4 unfavorable items). It encompasses five facets: (1) Observing, (2) Describing, (3) Acting with awareness, (4) Non-judging of inner experience, and (5) Non-reactivity to inner experience. Ailessphobia is measured using the Ailessphobia in Education Scale (AILPES), developed by Gezgin and Türk Kurtça (2025) and translated into Indonesian through translation procedures. This scale consists of 18 items (favorable). It comprises two main factors: (1) Academic self-efficacy anxiety and (2) Lack of academic confidence without AI.

Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh strategi guru dalam pembelajaran deep learning dan penggunaan Artificial Intelligence (AI) terhadap hasil belajar siswa melalui self-regulated learning (SRL) sebagai variabel mediasi di SMA Negeri 2 Balikpapan. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan jenis penelitian eksplanatori. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner, observasi, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan metode Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan bantuan perangkat lunak SmartPLS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan pembelajaran mendalam guru berpengaruh secara signifikan terhadap self-regulated learning dan hasil belajar siswa, namun tidak berpengaruh secara langsung terhadap hasil belajar siswa. Penggunaan AI juga terbukti berpengaruh signifikan terhadap self-regulated learning dan hasil belajar siswa. Selain itu, self-regulated learning berpengaruh secara signifikan terhadap hasil belajar. Hasil uji mediasi menunjukkan bahwa belajar yang dikontrol sendiri berfungsi sebagai mediator penuh pada hubungan antara guru strategi dan hasil belajar, serta berfungsi sebagai mediator parsial pada hubungan antara penggunaan AI dan hasil belajar. Oleh karena itu, dapat disimpulkan bahwa penguatan pembelajaran yang dikontrol sendiri merupakan komponen penting dalam penerapan strategi pembelajaran mendalam dan penggunaan AI untuk meningkatkan hasil belajar siswa

Abstract Spectral geometric methods provide mathematically interpretable representations of tissue morphology, yet their standalone performance in histopathology artificial intelligence has not been systematically evaluated. This study benchmarks purely spectral pipelines across representative digital pathology and spatial omics tasks relative to convolutional baselines. Spectral features derived from graph Laplacians, heat kernel signatures, spectral wavelet energy, Slepian concentrations, fractal descriptors, and persistent homology were extracted from histopathology patches using fixed-grid graphs. Features were processed using spectral neural operators and gradient boosting. Four tasks were evaluated: binary breast cancer classification (BreaKHis), multi-class glioblastoma region-patch classification, spatial transcriptomics prediction (10× Visium), and spot-wise denoising. Cross-validation and leave-one-slide-out strategies were applied. Metrics included accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), mean squared error, and Pearson correlation. Equivalence between spectral and CNN models was not established within the prespecified ±0.03 AUC margin. Purely spectral models achieved lower performance than convolutional baselines, with AUC differences of 0.12–0.23. The CNN→LGBM model achieved an accuracy of 0.83 ± 0.06, balanced accuracy of 0.73 ± 0.10, and AUC of 0.80 ± 0.13. Equivalence was not established within the prespecified margin. Fusion achieved balanced accuracy of 0.73 ± 0.08, equal to the CNN baseline mean balanced accuracy, without surpassing CNN AUC. Spatial transcriptomics prediction showed limited cross-slide generalization (Pearson correlation 0.06), whereas spot-wise denoising under sparse conditions showed competitive performance. Spectral geometric models do not outperform convolutional methods for classification or segmentation but provide complementary utility in denoising and sparse spatial settings.

documents.abstract: A durable agent can resume a consequential action while its authority changes and the action's external outcome remains uncertain. We study execution-time reliability of tool-using AI agents, isolating recovery decisions from language-model behavior. Checkpoint state, permission to dispatch, evidence of an external effect and permission to reconcile are distinct obligations. We present a finite conformance study that checks these obligations through histories scored against a provider effect ledger hidden from the recovering application. A prospectively frozen campaign executes 336 histories on native LangGraph and Temporal hosts, crossing 14 schedules, three provider contracts and four matched application policies. All 168 paired host cells have identical checked outcomes. Per host, retained-ledger reconciliation passes all 42 histories: 21 checked completions, 15 denials and six unknown outcomes with reservations retained. Cached retry, revalidation before retry and stable-key retry pass 30, 36 and 31 histories respectively. A separate 16-case component study of InfinityOS, an enterprise AI platform developed by Arya.ai, exercises exported authority, worker, recovery and settlement code over repository fakes. The results isolate the roles of current authority, provider contracts and retained observations in recovery, with safety, completion and unresolved obligations reported separately for the declared application profile.

Scientific computing increasingly relies on large language model-based agents for performance engineering tasks such as instrumentation, analysis, and workflow porting. However, agent effectiveness depends heavily on the surrounding harness, which typically relies on manually written skills and curated memory. This limits autonomous learning, forcing agents to repeatedly rediscover solutions rather than retain and reuse knowledge from prior executions. We introduce Phronix, a capability-centric learning paradigm that enables agentic harnesses to acquire, validate, and refine reusable capabilities from their own executions. Phronix operates through a predictor-validator-corrector loop: MCP tools and associated skills propose solutions, tool executions validate them, and observed outcomes refine the stored capabilities. It distills every observed interaction into a capability store and researches a failing task rather than abandoning it. First, such learned capabilities solve a recurring task on the first attempt in 93-95% of cases across every model, significantly reducing solution non-determinism and improving reliability. Second, Phronix turns an agent's own execution into 7.6-30.8 durable capabilities per task without user instruction, and creation falls below two once the needed capability exists. Third, warm-start runs consume only 0.38-0.40 million tokens per task, which is three to four times less than a single baseline attempt, while a cold-start costs no more than the baseline. On the 1000 Genome Pegasus workflow, instrumenting a production application for I/O performance analysis, Phronix passes all 11 correctness checks against six for the baseline harness, and also lifts the task solving rates of two cheaper models from 29% and 27% of SWE-bench tasks solved to 91% and 87%, respectively, matching the performance of the most expensive evaluated model.

Work-related stress is a leading occupational health concern, and a substantial literature suggests its consequences differ between women and men. Most of that literature, however, establishes that a difference exists without identifying the mechanism responsible. This study examined the physical and mental health consequences of work-related stress among employed women and men, and tested whether differences persisted after psychosocial working conditions were controlled. A comparative cross-sectional design was adopted. Data were collected from 101 full-time employees aged 25-50 in Bengaluru, India; the analytical sample comprised 100 participants (50 women, 50 men). A 50-item instrument assessed perceived stress, working conditions, physical symptoms, emotional wellbeing and coping. Physical health and emotional wellbeing scales showed good reliability (alpha = .83 and .86). Five of six hypotheses were unsupported: women and men did not differ in perceived stress (p = .584, d = -0.11), physical symptoms (p = .986, d = 0.004) or emotional wellbeing (p = .575, d = 0.11), and gender did not moderate the stress-health relationship. One significant difference emerged: men reported greater problem-focused coping (p < .001, d = -0.73), although the predicted difference in emotion-focused coping did not appear. Perceived stress correlated strongly with physical symptoms (r = .55) and emotional wellbeing (r = .62), explaining 30% and 39% of variance. Findings are consistent with a differential-exposure account: where working conditions were comparable, health consequences were comparable.

Enterprises increasingly rely on heterogeneous documents, relational databases, and analytical systems to support information retrieval and business decision-making. Integrating large language models (LLMs) with these sources introduces challenges in evidence reliability, analytical correctness, access control, and operational resilience. This paper presents PIU Smart Intelligence Agents, a security-aware multi-agent architecture designed to integrate enterprise document intelligence, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), semantic search, document summarization, naturallanguage-to-SQL analytics, key performance indicator (KPI) generation, and conversational AI within a common application and governance framework. The proposed architecture organizes specialized AI capabilities around shared services for authentication, authorization, request validation, provider integration, observability, and controlled data access. Its document-processing workflow encompasses file validation, text extraction, optical character recognition for scanned documents, normalization, chunking, embedding generation, and vector-based indexing. The structured-analytics workflow separates schema-aware query generation from SQL validation, restricted database execution, and result interpretation. The architecture also addresses provider compatibility, timeout handling, failure recovery, document lifecycle management, and traceability of generated outputs. The source implementation reports 1,242 automated tests passed and two integration tests skipped. These results are reported implementation evidence and have not been independently reproduced. The available evidence does not establish comprehensive external RAG benchmark performance, quantitative correctness across all agents, independently validated security effectiveness, or production-scale performance and recovery guarantees. Accordingly, this study presents an integrated engineering architecture and identifies a reproducible evaluation framework for assessing its effectiveness. The principal contribution is the systematic integration of heterogeneous enterprise AI capabilities with explicit governance and validation requirements, rather than the introduction of a new learning or retrieval algorithm. Future work should prioritize agent-specific correctness testing, retrieval and answer-quality benchmarks, adversarial security evaluation, controlled load testing, and recovery verification.

Dental imaging is fundamental to diagnosis, treatment planning, and follow-up in Oral Medicine and Maxillofacial Radiology. Although conventional radiographic interpretation remains dependent on professional expertise, diagnostic performance may be influenced by observer variability, image quality, workload, and the subtle nature of early pathological changes. The development of Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL), has introduced new approaches for automated analysis of dental and maxillofacial images. This narrative review discusses the evolution, principles, applications, clinical relevance, limitations, and future directions of deep learning in dental imaging, with emphasis on intraoral radiography, panoramic radiography, cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), and related imaging modalities. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated applications in dental caries detection, periodontal bone assessment, periapical lesion detection, tooth identification and numbering, jaw lesion analysis, anatomical segmentation, and treatment planning. More advanced architectures, including U-Net, residual networks, object-detection models, three-dimensional CNNs, and emerging transformer-based systems, have expanded the scope of automated image interpretation. However, the rapid growth of research has also highlighted important limitations, including small and heterogeneous datasets, inconsistent annotation, retrospective study designs, limited external validation, algorithmic bias, and difficulties in explaining model predictions. Importantly, high algorithmic accuracy does not necessarily translate into clinical effectiveness. Future research should therefore focus on diverse multicentre datasets, external and prospective validation, explainable AI, multimodal systems, ethical governance, and meaningful human-AI collaboration. Deep learning is most appropriately viewed as an adjunctive clinical decision-support technology that complements rather than replaces professional diagnostic judgment.

documents.abstract: Abstract— Preparing students for campus recruitment in a personalized and effective way is still difficult for most colleges. Typical placement systems deal mainly with administrative work such as registering students, storing company details, checking eligibility, and organizing recruitment drives, whereas interview training and companyspecific preparation are usually left to separate resources. This paper describes PlaceIntel, a web platform driven by multiple cooperating AI agents that unites central placement administration with tailored AI support for students. Four dedicated agents form the core of the system: a Mock Interview Agent, a Company Preparation Agent, a Company Research Agent, and a Skill Gap Analyzer. A Candidate Evaluation module additionally supports structured assessment during placement drives. The implementation relies on React, Java Spring Boot, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, LangGraph, and Gemini 3.6 Flash; authentication is handled with Spring Security and JWT, while Docker and AWS are used for deployment. The resulting architecture brings placement operations and AI-guided preparationtogether within a single modular design.
